items.claim: The rejection of a 19:15/19:16 cluster is substantively correct (shared lexeme, different grammatical role) but the row never quotes the Hebrew for this original-language distinction.
items.evidence: 19:15 closes ...וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב where וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ (nefesh) is the SUBJECT of the hunger-verb; 19:16 reads ...שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ... where נַפְשׁ֑וֹ (nafsho) is the OBJECT of the keeping-participle. Byte-collated from verse_map_oshb.json, this confirms the row's claim (shared lexeme נפש in two different syntactic roles, not a repeated construction) is correct. But the rationale and rejected_alternative state this only in English ('the same noun') with zero Hebrew quoted anywhere in the row -- insufficient engagement under the standing rule to quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim.

items.claim: The no-cluster verdict for 19:22 is likely still correct, but its stated Hebrew-echo grounds are internally inconsistent and arithmetically wrong, and no Hebrew is ever quoted.
items.evidence: 19:22's better-than-poor comparative (וְטֽוֹב רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב, tov rash me-ish kazav) that echoes 19:1's opening (טֽוֹב רָ֭שׁ..., tov rash) sits in 19:22's CLOSING colon, not its 'opening colon' as the rejected_alternative states -- the opening colon is תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ, about a man's kindness, which is what the row's own rationale correctly identifies as the first clause. Separately, the claim that '19:1 and 19:22 are three verses apart' is arithmetically false: 22 - 1 = 21 verses apart, not three. The independently-checked half of the claim (no word-bound shared token with 19:21 or 19:23) does hold at skeleton tier. No Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the row despite two original-language echo claims.

items.claim: The root-level distinction between 19:28 and 19:29 is correct (same root, process vs. penalty sense) but never quoted in the row.
items.evidence: 19:28 has מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (mishpat, 'the judicial process/justice') and 19:29 has שְׁפָטִ֑ים (shephatim, 'acts of judgment / penalties'); both share the root sh-p-t at byte tier, confirming the rejected_alternative's 'same root, two distinct senses (process vs. penalty)' claim. Correct substance, but zero Hebrew is quoted in rationale, device_notes, or rejected_alternative for a claim that is explicitly about shared Hebrew roots -- insufficient engagement under the same standing rule as P08-062.

items.claim: The rejection of a 20:5/20:6 cluster undercounts the cohesion evidence: it dismisses the shared noun as merely common, but the specific two-word doubling construction it forms is book-wide unique to this exact adjacent pair.
items.evidence: 20:5 reads ...בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה... (be-lev ish ve-ish tevunah) and 20:6 reads ...יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים... (yiqra ish chasdo ve-ish emunim) -- both verses use the identical word-bound doubling pattern ish ... ve-ish (a man ..., but a man ...). A book-wide word-bound skeleton sweep of the bare token (consonantal index, re-derived independently) shows ish alone in 53/915 verses -- genuinely too common on its own, matching the row's stated reason. But a sweep for the SAME VERSE containing BOTH the bare token AND its vav-prefixed double (ish and ve-ish together) returns exactly 2/915 verses book-wide, and those two verses are Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6 -- precisely the adjacent pair being rejected. The owner's cluster bar for C2 names 'construction runs' as qualifying cohesion evidence; a two-word doubling construction that is unique book-wide to exactly the two adjacent rows in question is stronger and more specific evidence than 'a common noun that recurs so often it cannot anchor a cluster,' and the row's rejected_alternative does not appear to have checked for it. This does not by itself mandate merging 20:5-20:6, but the rejection as written is grounded in an incomplete sweep.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep: same-verse 'ish'+'ve-ish' doubling = 2/915 verses (Prov.20.5, Prov.20.6 only)

items.claim: Mirrors P09-005: the rejection of a 20:5/20:6 cluster from the 20:6 side uses the same 'common noun' framing and misses the same book-wide-unique doubling construction.
items.evidence: 20:6 opens רָב אָדָ֗ם... (rav adam, 'many a man') and continues אִ֣ישׁ ... וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים (ish chasdo ... ve-ish emunim), reusing 20:5's own ish ... ve-ish doubling (be-lev ish ... ve-ish tevunah). Independently re-derived: bare word-bound 'ish' = 53/915 verses book-wide (confirms the row's 'recurs so often' premise for the bare noun), but the same-verse ish+ve-ish doubling pattern = exactly 2/915 verses, both of them Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6. As with P09-005, the row's dismissal treats this as a generic-noun echo rather than checking the specific, rare, shared construction -- the same underlying gap, argued from the 20:6 side of the same rejected pair.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep: same-verse 'ish'+'ve-ish' doubling = 2/915 verses (Prov.20.5, Prov.20.6 only)

items.claim: The מֶ֗לֶךְ opener collates byte-true and the 'no shared term' rejection of pairing with 20:9 holds at both seams.
items.evidence: Quoted opener מֶ֗לֶךְ (melekh) re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Prov.20.8. Word-bound skeleton comparison shows zero token overlap between 20:8 and 20:9, confirming the row's own claim. The row only discusses the forward seam (20:9); independently checking the backward seam (20:7) also shows zero word-bound overlap with 20:8, so the unaddressed seam does not conceal any undisclosed continuity -- the single_proverb boundary is clean on both sides.

items.claim: The יֵ֣שׁ opener collates byte-true and the 'share no lexeme' rejection of pairing with 20:16 holds at both seams.
items.evidence: Quoted opener יֵ֣שׁ (yesh) re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Prov.20.15. Word-bound skeleton comparison confirms zero token overlap with 20:16. The backward seam (20:14) was not discussed in the row but is independently confirmed to share zero tokens as well; the only echo across 20:14-20:15 is a shared VALUATION theme (price/worth), which the owner's granularity policy explicitly treats as insufficient glue on its own -- so the omission does not conceal genuine cohesion evidence.

items.claim: The 20:16/20:17 arav/arev split is a genuine pointed homograph (confirmed at codepoint level), correctly not counted as cluster evidence, and the K/Q disclosure matches pmarks.
items.evidence: 20:16's עָ֣רַב is AYIN + QAMATS + RESH + PATAH + BET (Qal perfect verb 'he stood surety'); 20:17's עָרֵ֣ב is AYIN + QAMATS + RESH + TSERE + BET (adjective 'sweet/pleasant') -- confirmed by direct unicode codepoint inspection of verse_map_oshb.json, not by rendering. Same three consonants, different vowel under the resh: a real homograph, matching the row's claim exactly. The row's Hebrew quote (לְֽקַח) re-collates at BYTE tier. Prov.20.16 is in the pmarks kq inventory (count 1); the verse's own bytes carry the unpointed ketiv נכרים inline before the pointed qere נָכְרִיָּ֣ה, matching the INLINE-KETIV pattern and the row's disclosed 'ketiv/qere note (pmarks, single witness)' language. No defect found.
